sections.content: The house sells for $450,000. The seller expects to walk away with $420,000. At closing, they receive $387,000. The look on their face—that mixture of confusion, disappointment, and suspicion directed at you—can kill your reputation faster than any online review.

Sellers don't know their actual proceeds. They see the sale price and mentally subtract their mortgage balance. They forget about agent commissions, closing costs, title fees, prorated taxes, and a dozen other deductions that eat into their bottom line. When they get the final number, it feels like a bait-and-switch, even when you did nothing wrong.
Setting expectations early isn't just good service—it's reputation protection.
The Proceeds Blindspot That Hurts Everyone

Most agents provide a rough net sheet at listing, then hope for the best. But rough estimates are dangerous. They don't account for negotiated repairs, buyer credits, or timing issues that affect prorations. And they certainly don't prepare sellers for the emotional impact of seeing that final number.

When sellers are surprised by their proceeds, they blame their agent. They question your commission. They wonder if you could have negotiated better. Even if the deal was fair, the surprise makes it feel unfair.
Professional Net Sheets Build Instant Credibility
The agents who win listings—and earn referrals—provide professional, detailed net proceeds estimates from day one. They show sellers:

items: Multiple net scenarios (best case, expected case, conservative case)
How different decisions affect the bottom line

sections.content: This transparency builds trust before the listing even hits the market.
When Sellers Know Their Numbers, They Make Better Decisions

Sellers who understand their actual proceeds make smarter choices. They price more realistically. They negotiate from a position of knowledge, not desperation. They're less likely to kill deals over minor repair requests because they understand the math.
The Tool That Sets You Apart

Top agents don't scribble numbers on napkins or send generic estimates. They provide polished, professional net proceeds calculations that sellers can review, share with their partners, and reference throughout the transaction.
This small step creates massive differentiation in a crowded market.
Remove Proceeds Surprises, Earn Seller Trust

Stop leaving sellers to guess about their money. When you provide clear, professional net proceeds estimates from the first meeting, you build trust, set realistic expectations, and protect your reputation all the way to closing.
